Presented on : 29-08-2018  Registered on : 29-08-2018

IN THE COURT OF THE I ADDL.CJM: BENGALURU  Dated this the 9th day of July 2024  Present: Shri Prakash.C.D, B.A., LL.B  I Addl. C.J.M BENGALURU.
 JUDGMENT U/s.355 Cr.P.C.,
Case No. C.C.No.23775/2018 Date of Offence 15/06/2016 onwards Name of complainant State by Vyalikaval Police  Station, Bengaluru.
 (By Learned  Sr. APP)
 V/s.
Name of accused Sagar Deep, s/o.Shivanna,
 35 yrs, NO.2, 2nd main, 6th  cross, Vyalikaval,
 Bengaluru.

(By Sri.GRS, Advocate)
Offences complained off U/s.498A r/w.34 of IPC  and Sec.3 & 4 of D.P.Act  2 C.C.No.23775/2018 Plea of accused Pleaded not guilty Final Order Accused is Acquitted Date of Order 09-07-2024  JUDGMENT

The charge sheet is submitted by the PSI of Vyalikaval P.S, against the accused for the offences punishable under section 498A r/w.34 of IPC and Sec.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.

1 2.

The prosecution case in brief is as under ; That the marriage of CW 1 with accused was solemnized on 15/06/2016 at Divya Convention Hall at Kunigal, at that time, accused demanded and received 10 grams finger ring, 24 grams bracelet, 30 grams gold chain as dowry.

Thereafter, while C.W.1 was residing along with accused at house No.2, 2nd main, 6th cross, accused has subjected the CW 1 to cruelty mentally and physically by suspecting her character and has treated CW-1 with cruelty.
It is further alleged that accused used to abuse and assault the CW 1 with hands and also demanded additional dowry of Rs.50 lakhs and thrown out her from the house.

Thus the accused has committed the offences punishable under section 498A r/w.34 of IPC and Sec.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
3.
The complainant has given complaint to the Vyalikaval police station and accordingly the police have registered the case in crime No.83/2018.
The concerned police after completing the investigation have filed charge sheet against the accused.
4. On the receipt of charge sheet the cognizance was taken.
The prosecution papers are given to the accused.
The charge was framed and read over to the accused .
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried, accordingly the plea of the accused was recorded.

5. The prosecution in support of their case have got examined the complainant/victim as Pw.1 and mahazar witness as PW 2 and father of the victim/complainant as PW 3 and got marked 6 documents at Ex.P.1 to 6.
6.
The statement of accused U/s 313 of Cr.P.C is dispensed with as there was no incriminating evidence against the accused.
The accused has not chosen to adduce defence evidence.
7. Heard arguments on both side.

8. The points that arise for consideration is as under :
1.

Whether prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that the marriage of CW 1 with accused was solemnized on 15/06/2016 at Divya Convention Hall at Kunigal, at that time, accused demanded and received 10 grams finger ring, 24 grams bracelet,
30 grams gold chain as dowry.

Thereafter, while C.W.1 was residing along with accused at house No.2, 2nd main, 6th cross, accused has subjected the CW 1 to cruelty mentally and physically by suspecting her character and has treated CW-1 with cruelty, that accused used to abuse and assault the CW 1 with hands and also demanded additional dowry of Rs.50 lakhs and thrown out her from the house.
Thus the accused has committed the offence punishable under section 498A r/w.34 of IPC and Sec.3 & 4 of D.P.Act and within my cognizance ?
2. What order ?

9. My answers to the above points are as under :
 Point No.1 : In the Negative.

Point No.2 : As per final order for the Varshitha vs Sagar Deep on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29909826/
2
following ;
REASONS 10. Point No.1 :- The allegation of the prosecution against the accused is that the marriage of CW 1 with accused was solemnized on 15/06/2016 at Divya Convention Hall at Kunigal

, at that time,
accused demanded and received 10 grams finger ring, 24 grams bracelet, 30 grams gold chain as dowry.

Thereafter, while C.W.1 was residing along with accused at house No.2, 2 nd main, 6th cross,
accused has subjected the CW 1 to cruelty mentally and physically by suspecting her character and has treated CW-1 with cruelty.
It is further alleged that accused used to abuse and assault the CW 1 with hands and also demanded additional dowry of Rs.50 lakhs and thrown out her from the house.

Thus the accused has committed the offence punishable under section 498A r/w.34 of IPC and Sec.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
11.

In order to prove the allegations made against the accused, prosecution has got examined the complainant/victim as Pw.1 and got marked the complaint, spot panchanama, Photographs and Invitation card at Ex.P.1 to 6 respectively.

12. On careful perusal of prosecution papers, it shows that the specific allegation made against the accused is that the accused ill-treated the CW 1 mentally and physically and also demanded additional dowry from her.
13. In view of the allegation made against the accused, at the first it is proper to look in to the evidence of Cw.1 who is the complainant/victim, who is examined as PW-1.

14. Further PW-1 who is the complainant and the victim of the alleged offences though supported the case of the prosecution during chief examination alleging ill- treatment of accused physically and mentally and also demanding additional dowry, but during the course of cross examination, she has given clear goby to the case of the prosecution and has deposed as hereunder :

"       
   ,      
    ,   
   ,   ,    
    ,    
        ........
15. PW-1 being the complainant/victim has completely turned hostile and not supported the prosecution case and deposed that there was no any offences made by the accused.

3 16.

sentences.text: Further the prosecution has got examined one of the mahazar witness CW 2 as PW2 and father of the victim / complainant as PW 3

, though they have supported the case of the prosecution, in view of the hostile evidence of PW 1, their evidence will not help the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
17. Though the learned A.P.P treating the PW 1 as hostile and cross examined the PW 1, but nothing is uttered by the PW 1 in order to support the prosecution case.

19. In the present case on hand the important material witness/victim herself has turned hostile and has not supported the case of prosecution and accordingly prosecution has utterly failed to prove the case.

The prayer of learned Sr.APP to issue summons to other witnesses is Rejected as no purpose will be served by issuing summons to other witnesses, as the complainant/victim herself has turned hostile to the case of the prosecution.
Hence, it cannot be held that the accused has committed the offences punishable under section 498A r/w.34 of IPC and Sec.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
Accordingly I answered this point in the Negative.

20. Point No.2 :- In view the findings given in point No.1, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C accused is hereby Acquitted for the offences punishable under section 498A r/w.34 of IPC and Sec.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
The bail bond and surety bond of accused stands canceled after appeal period is over.

(This judgment is dictated to stenographer directly on computer, typed by her,
corrected and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 9 th day of July 2024)
(PRAKASH.C.D) I Addl.
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru
